label: Claude Opus 5.5
output:
I've been tagged on Kavya's post a lot since yesterday, so I'll respond here instead of in the comments. @Kavya

Kavya and I were in Foundry91 Cohort 4 together. Before demo day in March, she sat with me till 1am in our Koramangala office fixing a Razorpay webhook mess on DabbaDost. I haven't forgotten that, and nothing in this post changes how I think about her or SitterNest.

Two engineers from her team joined us on 3 Nov. I won't name them. They didn't sign up for a public discussion, and I'd ask everyone to leave them out of it.

First, the part I got wrong. I knew where they worked from day one. I should have called Kavya before making the offers, not after. I messaged her once the second offer was accepted, and by then it was a done deal. Founder to founder, that's not how I'd want to find out either. That's on me, and I'm sorry, Kavya.

A few things I do need to correct, mainly because numbers get repeated:

• Nobody from our side DMed anyone. We posted a backend developer opening on our LinkedIn page and on Instahyre on 14 Sept, open to anyone. The first engineer applied on his own on 19 Sept. The second came through his referral about two weeks later.
• The offer was 22% over their current CTC, not 40%.
• We do have an ESOP pool. It's small, but it's real and has been on paper since January.

I'm not saying this to win an argument. I'm saying it because "40%" and "no ESOPs" will keep doing the rounds otherwise, and that's not fair to either company.

The bigger issue is real though. We're 11 startups in one batch, mostly hiring from the same small pool in HSR and Koramangala. This will happen again, to someone else, probably soon.

So here's a simple rule I'd like to suggest for the cohort: if you're interviewing someone from another batch company, give that founder a heads-up before you make the offer. You're not asking permission, just giving a heads-up. People should be free to move, and founders shouldn't find out from a resignation email. A heads-up costs one phone call and saves a friendship. I'm happy to follow it first.

Kavya, coffee or a call, this week, whenever you're okay with it. I'd much rather sort this out over filter coffee than in a comment thread.

Thanks to everyone who reached out. Please don't pile on anyone in the comments, including Kavya.

---

This comes to about 420 words and roughly 2,400 characters, so it fits within LinkedIn's limit. I left out the blue tick detail on purpose. Mentioning it publicly would read as a dig. Saying you messaged her too late makes the same point and keeps the focus on what you did wrong. Replace "@Kavya" with her actual tag when you post.
